name: Cover letter – proposal for underwriting services
text: Goldman, Sachs & Co. is extremely pleased to submit our response to your request for proposal for underwriting services. We place tremendous value in our investment banking relationships and view this opportunity as a significant step in providing broad based, high quality investment banking services to Presbyterian Healthcare Services. Presbyterian's recent revised outlook by Moody's, demonstrative of the significant progress the system has made towards an upgrade to the Aa category, comes at a time when the system IJ faces growing regional competitive pressures. This, combined with Presbyterian's projected capital needs, creates a complex and challenging context for the development of a capital plan. ' This is exactly the sort of challenge we enjoy and excel at. We feel the skills and capacities we I ~ .1 would bring to Presbyterian are well suited to this situation. These strengths include: leadership in healthcare finance, extensive experience working with integrated healthcare systems, a teamwork approach, unique idea generation, unparalleled auction rate performance, tailored ll _j derivative products, and a sincere desire to work with Presbyterian. We hope that this proposal helps to demonstrate the commitment and depth of services that we are prepared to provide Presbyterian. We believe our unique combination of experience, resources, and enthusiasm is a platform that would make for a productive and successful longterm relationship. On behalf of the Goldman Sachs team, we very much hope to have the opportunity to serve Presbyterian and help the organization achieve its financial and strategic goals. Should you have any questions or desire additional information, please do not hesitate to contact our team leader Sue Benz at (212) 902-6437.

name: Firm overview and business principles
text: Goldman Sachs is a leading global investment banking and securities finn, pro,·iding a full range of investing, I advisory, and financing services worldwide to a substantial and diversified client base, which includes governments, corporations, financial institutions and indi\·iduals. The finn was founded in 1869 as a commercial paper dealer, a product the firm created. After more than a century as a private parhwrship, the firm became a public company in 1999. The firm is headquartered in New York and maintains offices in other financial centers around the world. I Goldman Sachs currently has 44 offices in 23 countries. The finn's Not-for-Profit Healthcare Group consists of 19 fulltime professionals who are supported by members of specialty finance groups such as credit, derivatives, short-term, quantitative and tax services. Goldman Sachs prides itself on providing complete, broad based, intensive coverage for our clients, regardless of where they are in their capital cycle. While we have recently added a number of new clients, many of our relationships span decades. We maintain these relationships by providing a complete and varied range of services, by I being a product innovator and market leader, and by focusing on what is best for the client rather than what produces the next trade. The Firm's Business Principles govern our approach to all of our business activities. As our Business Principles I indicate, "Our clients' interests always come first Our experience shows that if we serve our clients welt our own success will follow." Accordingly, finance teams assigned to each particular client are charged with accessing and directing the Firm's vast resources in the structuring and execution of each transaction. This philosophy of investment I banking is the hallmark of our success in providing superior service to each of our nonprofit healthcare clients. We have included the Firm's Business Principles as Appendix A We would be proud to add Presbyterian Health Services to our list of clients.

text: TO Goldman Sachs' focus within the healthcare industry has remained intensely oriented towards healthcare systems, I many of which are complex integrated healthcare organizations. name: Integrated approach across service areas
text: Although each of these clients is unique in its needs and required a customized capital formation strategy, all found that an integrated approach created the greatest level of financing success. As explained below, Goldman Sachs is a leader and innovator in each of the service areas desired by Presbyterian: capital formation, underwriting; remarketing; auction agent/broker-dealer services; derivative product development and execution; strategic advisory services; and use of credit enhancement . However, as illustrated in the Trinity Healthcare case study which concludes this section, it is through the integration of these areas of expertise into a comprehensive, capital management strategy that we are able to provide our clients with the greatest value.

name: Capital formation strategies and Capital Structure Management Model
text: FORMATION STRATEGI As indicated above, we take the long view of capital formation. An integrated approach toward capital planning incorporates not only the immediate needs of an organization, but its long-term goals, and includes variables such as the optimal cost of capitat organizational strategic initiatives requiring investment, desired rating category, and asset liability management. Our Capital Structure Management (CSM) Model is the central tool used in providing this service. The CSM model is a proprietary Monte Carlo simulation-based capital struchlring and optimization system developed specifically for the complex needs of the firm's largest and most prestigious corporate, tax-exempt and sovereign clients. Goldman Sachs also uses the model internally to evaluate debt and investment strategies. Our model provides CFOs and Treasurers with a plan for constructing optimal debt and investment portfolios based upon their cost/risk objectives and existing constraints. The model can assist Presbyterian in determining the type of debt to issue (e.g., maturity, call/put features, fixed versus floating), the exposure of Presbyterian's overall liabilities to movements in interest rates, the impact of derivative securities such as swaps, as well as optimal refunding strategies for existing debt issues. It has the capability to evaluate Presbyterian's investment exposures vis-a-vis the debt portfolio and help devise strategies to manage this risk and can incorporate pension liabilities into the overall liability portfolio and assess the impact of the liability on risk management.
